title: Chapter 3 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of interactive containers, inspection, monitoring, file operations, and advanced container management!

questions.question: Which command runs a new interactive Bash shell inside an existing container named 'web'?
questions.explanation: `docker exec -it web bash` starts a new Bash process interactively. `docker attach` connects to the main process, not a new shell.

questions.question: `docker exec` can only run commands in a stopped container.
questions.explanation: `docker exec` requires the container to be running. A stopped container has no running processes to attach to.

questions.question: What does the `-t` flag do in `docker exec -it`?
questions.explanation: `-t` allocates a terminal driver, allowing proper interactive shell behaviour. `-i` keeps STDIN open.

questions.question: How do you safely detach from a container using `docker attach` without stopping it?
questions.explanation: `Ctrl+P` `Ctrl+Q` detaches without killing the main process. `Ctrl+C` would send SIGINT and likely stop the container.

questions.question: What is the main difference between `docker attach` and `docker exec`?
options: `attach` starts a new process, `exec` connects to the main process
`attach` connects to the main process, `exec` starts a new process
`attach` requires the container to be stopped
questions.explanation: `docker attach` hooks into PID 1, while `docker exec` launches a completely new process.

questions.question: Which command shows low‑level JSON metadata for a container?
questions.explanation: `docker inspect` returns a JSON array with all container details.

questions.question: To extract only the IP address of a container using `docker inspect`, you would use the template `{{.NetworkSettings._____}}`.
questions.explanation: The Go template path for the IP address is `.NetworkSettings.IPAddress`.

questions.question: What does `docker stats` display?
options: The full process list inside a container
Real‑time CPU, memory, network and I/O usage of containers
questions.explanation: `docker stats` gives a live stream of resource consumption.

questions.question: `docker stats --no-stream` shows a single snapshot of resource usage.
questions.explanation: Adding `--no-stream` disables the continuous refresh, printing one set of values and exiting.

questions.question: Which command shows the running processes inside a container?
questions.explanation: `docker top` lists the processes of a container without needing to exec into it.

questions.question: How do you copy a file `report.html` from the container `app` to the local directory?
questions.explanation: The syntax is `docker cp SRC DEST`. To get a file out, the container path is the source.

questions.question: `docker cp` can copy files between two running containers.
questions.explanation: `docker cp` works between host and container, not directly container‑to‑container.

questions.question: What does `docker commit my-container my-image:v2` do?
options: Creates a new container from my-image:v2
Saves the current state of my-container as a new image tagged my-image:v2
Deletes my-container and replaces it with my-image:v2
questions.explanation: `docker commit` captures a container’s filesystem changes into a new image.

questions.question: Why is `docker commit` generally not recommended for building production images?
options: It results in images that are too small
It does not record how the image was created, making it less reproducible
It cannot be pushed to Docker Hub
It only works on Windows containers
questions.explanation: Commit lacks a build history (Dockerfile), making it opaque and hard to recreate.

questions.question: Which command renames a container from 'old_name' to 'new_name'?
questions.explanation: `docker rename` is the dedicated command. `docker tag` is for images.

questions.question: Setting a restart policy of `--restart=always` means the container will restart even if you explicitly run `docker stop`.
questions.explanation: `always` restarts the container unless the daemon stops. `unless-stopped` respects a manual stop.

questions.question: Which flag limits a container to 512 MB of RAM?
questions.explanation: `--memory` (or `-m`) sets the memory limit. The value can be `512m` for megabytes.

questions.question: What does `--cpus=2` restrict?
options: The number of container instances allowed
The number of CPU cores the container can use
The priority of the container in the scheduler
questions.explanation: `--cpus` specifies how much of the host CPU a container can use. `2` means 2 CPU cores.

questions.question: To remove all stopped containers in one command, you use `docker container _____`.
questions.explanation: `docker container prune` removes all stopped containers. It’s a quick cleanup command.

questions.question: You want to run a container and automatically delete it when it stops. Which flag do you add?
questions.explanation: `--rm` ensures the container is automatically removed after it exits.

questions.question: `docker stats` works on stopped containers.
questions.explanation: `docker stats` only shows running containers because a stopped container consumes no resources.

questions.question: How can you see the environment variables set inside a container using `docker inspect`?
questions.explanation: The environment variables are stored under `.Config.Env`. The template syntax is needed to extract them.
